title: Add break-glass verification override guardrails + required audit annotations
author: Kevin Osei
release_notes: Private/on-prem: Adds cluster policy guardrails for break-glass verification override usage, requiring standardized audit annotations and limiting who can request/approve override in-cluster.
description: Title: Add break-glass verification override guardrails + required audit annotations. Context: As part of offline bundle signature verification, the installer now supports a policy-gated break-glass flag (see redwood-private-installer pr-24979). This PR adds cluster-side guardrails so that (1) break-glass cannot be enabled silently, (2) use is attributable and exportable via audit logs, and (3) only approved operators can authorize it. Summary of changes: (A) Adds a Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate + Constraint enforcing required annotations whenever break-glass is enabled via the Redwood Private install metadata ConfigMap (redwood-private/install-metadata) or Helm values rendered into that ConfigMap. Required annotations: redwood.ai/break-glass-ticket (SUP-/INT-/customer ticket id), redwood.ai/break-glass-reason (freeform, min 20 chars), redwood.ai/break-glass-approved-by (corporate email), redwood.ai/break-glass-approved-at (RFC3339 timestamp), redwood.ai/break-glass-expires-at (RFC3339; must be <= 72h from approved-at). Optional but recommended: redwood.ai/break-glass-approver-role (Security|ReleaseEng|SRE). (B) Adds a second constraint that denies enabling break-glass unless the requesting subject is in the allowlisted RBAC group (redwood:break-glass-approvers) or is a ServiceAccount with label redwood.ai/purpose=private-installer and bound to ClusterRole redwood-private-break-glass-approver. (C) Adds a policy exception mechanism for dev/test clusters only: if Namespace has label redwood.ai/environment=dev and redwood.ai/policy-exceptions contains break-glass-guardrails, constraints run in "warn" mode and include a warning message; default remains "deny" for all other environments. (D) Adds a small conftest test suite covering: missing annotations, malformed timestamps, expiry > 72h, approver not allowlisted, and the dev warn-only path. Why this approach: We want verification to fail closed by default but still support emergency installs when signatures cannot be verified due to environmental constraints (time skew, trust store mismatch, etc.). The installer already logs local audit markers; these policies ensure the cluster also has consistent, queryable attribution for any break-glass activation, and prevent accidental enablement by automation. Implementation notes: Policies target the install-metadata ConfigMap because it is the canonical place we already read for support bundles and audit export mapping. We intentionally avoid requiring outbound connectivity or external approvals (air-gapped), but we require the metadata fields that support and security will request during incident response and compliance evidence collection. Files / areas changed: policy/gatekeeper/templates/redwoodprivatebreakglass_annotations_template.yaml; policy/gatekeeper/constraints/redwoodprivatebreakglass_annotations_constraint.yaml; policy/gatekeeper/templates/redwoodprivatebreakglass_approver_template.yaml; policy/gatekeeper/constraints/redwoodprivatebreakglass_approver_constraint.yaml; rbac/clusterroles/redwood-private-break-glass-approver.yaml; rbac/clusterrolebindings/redwood-private-break-glass-approver-binding.yaml; tests/conftest/break_glass_annotations_test.rego; tests/fixtures/install-metadata-configmap.yaml; README.md (break-glass section). Illustrative snippet (ConstraintTemplate logic, shortened): "violation[{"msg": msg}] { input.review.kind.kind == "ConfigMap"; input.review.object.metadata.name == "install-metadata"; input.review.object.metadata.namespace == "redwood-private"; input.review.object.data["break_glass_enabled"] == "true"; missing := {"redwood.ai/break-glass-ticket", "redwood.ai/break-glass-reason", "redwood.ai/break-glass-approved-by", "redwood.ai/break-glass-approved-at", "redwood.ai/break-glass-expires-at"} - {k | input.review.object.metadata.annotations[k]}; count(missing) > 0; msg := sprintf("break-glass enabled but missing required annotations: %v", [missing]) }". Testing: make policy-lint; make test-conftest; validated against a local kind cluster with Gatekeeper v3.14. CI: gatekeeper-schema-check, conftest, yamllint all green. Rollout: This is a no-op unless Gatekeeper is installed (standard for regulated Private installs). For existing clusters, apply templates/constraints first (will only affect future changes to install metadata). Related: ENG-4824 (break-glass design), ENG-4829 (audit event schema), SUP-31977 (support guidance).
commits: Add Gatekeeper constraint template for required break-glass audit annotations
Enforce approver allowlist / RBAC group for break-glass enablement
Add conftest coverage for break-glass guardrails
Document break-glass policy requirements and dev exceptions
conversation: Marcus Lin (review): Can we tighten the schema so expires-at is always present and bounded? Also, confirm we’re not allowing arbitrary subjects to set these annotations (otherwise someone can self-approve). Kevin Osei (author): Updated template to require expires-at and added <=72h bound relative to approved-at. Added a separate approver constraint: deny unless user is in redwood:break-glass-approvers or installer SA bound to redwood-private-break-glass-approver. Allison Grant (review): Annotation names look good, but please align with logging redaction guidance (don’t force PII). Can we avoid requiring a full name? Kevin Osei: Using corporate email only; reason field is freeform but we recommend excluding customer identifiers; added README guidance. Ethan Park (review): Installer writes install-metadata—will this block initial install? We need a path where break-glass is off by default. Kevin Osei: Constraint only triggers when break_glass_enabled==true. Default install-metadata has it false; initial install unaffected. Connor O'Brien (review): Please add a warn-only mechanism for dev clusters. Kevin Osei: Added label-based exception for redwood.ai/environment=dev with enforcementAction=warn and explicit warning message; production remains deny. Final: Marcus approved after seeing tests for malformed timestamps and allowlist enforcement; Allison approved after README update. CI had one failure due to Gatekeeper schema mismatch; reran after fixing apiVersion and it passed.
